hypothesis: The frozen 256-token state representation can support spectral and wave-speed OOD generalization even when the exact spatial Laplacian is not supplied, provided the transition is constrained to a learnable local operator plus a context-inferred scalar coefficient.

learned_operator.input_data: decoded states from frozen discrete tokens only
learned_operator.kernel_fit: ridge least squares mapping midpoint displacement u_avg=(u_t+u_t+1)/2 to observed velocity derivative (v_t+1-v_t)/dt over all quantized training transitions
learned_operator.time_update_prior: velocity-Verlet form is supplied; acceleration is scale * learned_kernel(u)
learned_operator.sequence_scale_inference: closed-form least-squares scalar from the two observed quantized context transitions
learned_operator.rollout: recursive with requantization to the same 256-token codebook after every predicted step

frozen_pass_rule: PASS only if every one of the 3 fresh replicates has requantized rollout MSE ratio < 1.0 versus raw-state persistence on ID h8, spectrum-OOD h3, and combined-OOD h3. No retry or replacement of a failed replicate. Kernel similarity to the true Laplacian and inferred-scale correlations are secondary diagnostics only.
claim_limit: A pass would demonstrate learned local-operator extrapolation in this synthetic wave benchmark from quantized trajectories. It would not establish general scientific-law discovery because the 3x3 locality and velocity-Verlet temporal form are supplied priors.
